Maintenance Procedures — Overhead Lines
Document No.: Ins-003-r1a
Changing a single tension insulator on 132 and 220 kV towers, with the circuit de-energised
Issued to: Extra High Voltage Networks
Document status: Approved
Document approval date: 6/2/2000
Next review date: 2/2005
Page No.: 1/1

sections_target.text: Introduction

This document was first produced in 1996 in English under No. LI-TL-006-r0 with the assistance of Mr. Tom C. from the Canadian Project and Eng. Abdel Hadi from the Greater Cairo Extra High Voltage Sector, using documents from Ontario Hydro, the Canadian company, and also the Lines Department at the Networks Training Centre of the Authority's Training Department. It was reviewed with the knowledge of the regions and approved by the Central Committee for Network Affairs on 2/9/96. For wider benefit, the document was translated into Arabic under No. Ins-003-r1a with the assistance of Middle Delta, then put into the new format of the Maintenance Procedures Information System document template.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be obtained.
Earth the work location from both sides.
A safety helmet must be worn.
A safety belt must be worn.
Tools and Equipment Used
Tools and Quantities
Hand line — 1
Earth cables (their size and number depend on the value of the existing short-circuit current)
Earth stick — 1
Nylon slings or steel wire slings capable of withstanding the tension in the conductor — 3
Chain hoist capable of withstanding the tension in the conductor — 1
13 mm diameter rope (1/2 inch) for tying operations
Split sheave (4 inch) — 2
Insulator loading hanger — 1
19 mm diameter rope, 60 m long (3/4 inch, 200 ft long) — 1
Slack hoist or any other mechanical lifting tool — 1
Shackle capable of withstanding the tension in the conductor, fitted in the hole of the insulator end plate — 1
Scaffold to allow access to the conductor when fitting the grip (come-along) and the chain hoist on the conductor — 1
Replacement insulators of sound size
Work Steps to be Carried Out
Preparation procedures:

rows: Calculate the tension in the conductor in order to determine the sizes of the equipment required.
Obtain a work permit for the circuit.
Fit the hand line on the tower arm or leg in a suitable place for raising the equipment.
Fit the slack hoist on the tower leg near the tower base, for raising and lowering the equipment.
Test for absence of voltage on the circuit, then carry out earthing in accordance with the approved earthing procedures.
Fit the scaffold by placing the scaffold hook on the conductor and tying the scaffold chains to the tower arm angles from below (see Figure 1).
Test the porcelain insulators to determine the total number of damaged discs to be changed.

Fit a nylon sling or a steel wire sling at the tower arm and around the tension plate in which the insulator string is fixed. The nylon sling must be protected from cutting by the metal angles of the tower.
Note:

The sling is connected to the insulator tension plate by a shackle if the hole in the tension plate is large enough to fit the shackle. The shackle and the sling must be strong enough to withstand the tension in the conductor.
Fit a grip (come-along) on the conductor between the scaffold hook and the end of the conductor at the insulator string.
Connect the end of the chain hoist to the sling and the chain hoist hook to the grip (come-along) on the conductor. See Figure 1.

sections_target.text: Figure No. 1 — Installing the Rigging
Fitting the Equipment
Changing single insulators:

rows: Tie the insulator string with the chain hoist. Leave the insulators to be replaced free, without tying.
Tighten the chain hoist until there is enough slack to remove the damaged insulators.
Change the damaged discs, then untie the insulator tying rope from the chain hoist.
Slack off the chain hoist, making sure the insulator holes and fixing bolts are correctly positioned.
Remove the equipment and lower it to the ground.
Work steps: Changing a complete insulator string:
Fit another grip (come-along) on the conductor, then connect a split sheave to this grip; see Figure 2.
Fit another sheave on the tower arm near the insulator tension plate, using a sling.
Tie the 19 mm diameter rope (3/4 inch) to the third disc from the conductor side, then pass this rope through the two sheaves as shown in Figure 2.
Wrap a rope around the end of the conductor and the chain hoist to avoid bending the conductor near the grip.
Tighten the chain hoist to slacken the insulator string.
Connect the tension rope to the slack hoist, then tighten the rope to pull the end of the insulator from the conductor side.
Disconnect the insulator string from the conductor side.
Slack off the tension rope to allow the insulator string to descend vertically downwards.
Untie the rope from the sheave at the conductor grip.
Fit the insulator loading hanger below the third disc from the tower arm.
Tie the rope to the insulator loading hanger, leaving some slack in the rope as shown in Figure 3. Load the rope so that the insulator can be removed from the tower arm.
Remove the insulator from the loading rope and reverse these steps.
Reverse these procedures to fit the replacement string and return it to its normal position.

sections_target.text: Safety Summary:

The following hazards and precautions are emphasised to explain the safety procedures relating to this work. Other hazards, which are specific to the work site itself or of a general nature, must be identified during preparation and before starting work.
Hazards — Precautions
Electrical — Obtain a work permit for the circuit.
— Test that the circuit is isolated, then earth it using the approved earthing procedures.
Mechanical — Calculate the tension in the conductor to test the loading of the equipment.
— Make sure the insulator holes and bolts are correctly positioned.
Working at heights — Use an approved fall protection system.
Communications — Use a good and clear method of communication for all the work team.

uncertain_terms.note: 'مستر/توم سى' rendered as 'Mr. Tom C.'; the surname is given only as an initial in the source.
'بمعرقة المناطق' appears to be a typo for 'بمعرفة المناطق' ('with the knowledge of the regions'); rendered as 'with the knowledge of the regions'.
Date kept as written in the source ('2/9/96'); presumably 2 September 1996.
'مساكة (زرجينة)' rendered as 'grip (come-along)', the linework grip tool.
No quantity is stated for the 13 mm rope in section 15; translated without a quantity.
Step 29:10:0 is garbled in the source ('بشد ومش السلسلة'); rendered as 'Tighten the chain hoist to slacken the insulator string'.
'فك النهمات' in step 29:4:0 appears to be a typo for 'فك المهمات' ('remove the equipment'); rendered as 'Remove the equipment'.
'الأدوات الكمية' rendered as 'Tools and Quantities' (tools with their quantities).
